system:
You are the test planner of a network change-validation pipeline. Given the change ticket, the
intent analysis and the configuration diff, write a change-specific test plan that (a) checks every effect the ticket
promises and (b) checks that nothing else that the diff could affect has changed (use expect "unchanged").
Also consider emulation-only risks: MTU (mtu probes), failover timers (conv), link load after path changes (load).
Typed test language (JSON objects; use ONLY these types and only names that exist):
  {"t":"reach","src":HOST,"dst":HOST|ROUTER,"svc":SVC|"*","expect":"allow"|"deny"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"path","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"via":ROUTER,"expect":true|false}
  {"t":"route","dev":ROUTER,"prefix":"a.b.c.d/n","expect":"present"|"absent"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"adj","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"expect":"up"|"down"|"unchanged"}          (OSPF adjacency on a link)
  {"t":"mtu","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"size":1500|9000,"expect":"pass"|"fail"}  (DF probe, emulation tier)
  {"t":"conv","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_s":3}                               (failover time of a link, emulation)
  {"t":"load","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_pct":90}                            (link utilisation, emulation)
  {"t":"like","host":HOST,"as":HOST}     (after a VLAN move / re-addressing: host has exactly the same access as the
                                          reference host, towards and from every other host and service)
SVC is one of: icmp, tcp/22, tcp/25, tcp/80, tcp/443, tcp/5432, udp/53.
Reply with JSON only: {"tests": [ ... ]}

Tenant B's public web (10.201.1.0/24) is being moved to a CDN: remove it from PL_PUBLIC on border1 and border2 so it is no longer announced to the WAN. wan-user1 will lose access to web-b1; web-a1 stays published.

INTENT ANALYSIS:
{"ticket_says": "Remove Tenant B's public web prefix (10.201.1.0/24) from the PL_PUBLIC prefix-list on border1 and border2 so it is no longer announced to the WAN, because it is moving to a CDN. wan-user1 will lose access to web-b1; web-a1 (Tenant A) must stay published.", "goal": "Withdraw the Tenant B web prefix 10.201.1.0/24 from WAN advertisement on both border routers by removing it from PL_PUBLIC, while keeping Tenant A's web prefix published.", "change_type": "bgp_policy", "scope": ["border1", "border2", "PL_PUBLIC", "10.201.1.0/24", "web-b1", "web-a1", "wan-user1"], "expected_effects": ["10.201.1.0/24 is no longer permitted by PL_PUBLIC on border1", "10.201.1.0/24 is no longer permitted by PL_PUBLIC on border2", "10.201.1.0/24 is no longer announced to the WAN", "wan-user1 can no longer reach web-b1", "web-a1 remains published and reachable"], "must_not_change": ["web-a1's prefix stays in PL_PUBLIC and remains announced to the WAN"], "confidence": "high"}

CONFIG DIFF:
border1 | ip prefix-list PL_PUBLIC | - ip prefix-list PL_PUBLIC seq 5 permit 10.101.1.0/24
border2 | ip prefix-list PL_PUBLIC | - ip prefix-list PL_PUBLIC seq 5 permit 10.101.1.0/24

TOPOLOGY (2-hop around changed devices): devices ['border1', 'border2', 'leaf1', 'leaf2', 'leaf3', 'leaf4', 'leaf5', 'leaf6', 'oob', 'spine1', 'spine2', 'wan']; hosts ['wan-user1']; links ['leaf1--spine1 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf1--spine2 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf2--spine1 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf2--spine2 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf3--spine1 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf3--spine2 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf4--spine1 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf4--spine2 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf5--spine1 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf5--spine2 (40000 Mbps)', 'leaf6--spine1 (10000 Mbps)', 'leaf6--spine2 (10000 Mbps)', 'border1--spine1 (100000 Mbps)', 'border2--spine1 (100000 Mbps)', 'oob--spine1 (1000 Mbps)', 'border1--spine2 (100000 Mbps)', 'border2--spine2 (100000 Mbps)', 'oob--spine2 (1000 Mbps)', 'border1--wan (10000 Mbps)', 'border2--wan (10000 Mbps)']
Hosts: wan-user1(198.18.0.10,wan,mtu 1500), web-a1(10.101.1.10,tenantA-web,mtu 9000), stage-a1(10.101.2.10,tenantA-stage,mtu 9000), app-a1(10.102.1.10,tenantA-app,mtu 9000), db-a1(10.103.1.10,tenantA-db,mtu 9000), web-b1(10.201.1.10,tenantB-web,mtu 9000), stage-b1(10.201.2.10,tenantB-stage,mtu 9000), db-b1(10.203.1.10,tenantB-db,mtu 9000), dns-dc1(10.30.0.10,shared-dns,mtu 9000), backup1(10.31.0.10,shared-backup,mtu 9000), noc1(10.99.0.10,noc,mtu 1500)

The diff contradicts the ticket: web-a1 would be withdrawn and web-b1's status is unaffected. The plan checks both the ticket's promises and what the diff actually does, so the mismatch surfaces as failures.
